**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part**: Sugarcane leaf blade, close-up
- **Color pattern**: Distinct alternating green and pale yellow/yellow longitudinal bands/streaks running parallel to the leaf veins along the length of the blade
- **Texture/shape**: Leaf appears structurally normal — no twisting, curling, necrosis, or discrete lesions
- **Key feature**: Multiple yellow streaks interspersed with green tissue, running parallel to the veins from one end to the other

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Brown_Spot / Yellow_Spot**: No discrete circular/elliptical lesions — ruled out
- **Leaf_Scald**: No white pencil line, no scorched/curling margins — ruled out
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: No twisted or malformed leaf tissue, no chlorosis at base — ruled out
- **Sett_Rot / Grassy_Shoot**: Not applicable to a single normal-looking leaf — ruled out
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Yellow_Leaf shows midrib yellowing; here the yellow is spread across the entire blade in multiple streaks, not just the midrib
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Mosaic typically shows irregular mottling/blotching
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: The hallmark is longitudinal yellow-green streaks running parallel to the veins — this matches precisely what is seen: distinct pale yellow elongated streaks alternating with green tissue, running the full length of the blade parallel to the venation

The streak pattern is the defining feature here — regular, vein-parallel yellow streaking across the blade is classic for Streak Mosaic (SCSMV).
